Everything else re-verified on the current code: I re-ran the fetched official andyzoujm/representation-engineering ClusterMeanRepReader head-to-head on gpt2 and BLME reproduces it to max abs 4.77e-07 / max rel 1.04e-07 across all 12 block layers (0.745291 ... 14.097246); ln_f(hooked layers[-1]) still reproduces HF hidden_states[-1] to 0.0e+00 on gpt2 / pythia-70m / distilgpt2; the per-pair agreement statistic reproduces independently to 1e-8 (-0.0022900 overall, +0.013709 at max-norm layer 11); and a generator dataset works. paper_reason: Zou et al. 2023 publish no direction-intrinsic scalar: no cosine value, no reading-vector norm, and the only mean-difference result (Figure 12) is a bar chart with no table. defects: COMPARABILITY: max_norm_layer is rho +0.997 with n_layers (up from +0.994 pre-fix) and equals n_layers-1 in 9 of 10 panel models -- it carries essentially no information beyond depth. This is the item the coordinator asked about: yes, register a normalized twin, but a depth FRACTION is necessary and not sufficient here, because the fraction is itself the constant 1.0 for 9 of 10 models. The honest options are to drop the column or to report the argmax over a depth-normalised profile (e.g. norm/sqrt(d_model) after per-model standardisation of the layer profile).

SIGNAL: pair_direction_cos_mean is now correct and near-empty -- [-0.060, +0.007] for 9 of 10 models. The 5 bundled pairs never agree on a direction at any scale tested, so the reported mean vector is a cancellation of near-orthogonal per-pair directions.

CONTROL: a random-init GPT-2 returns max_norm_layer 11 (identical to trained) and mean_vector_norm within 11% of trained. No random-weight baseline, bootstrap direction stability or held-out accuracy is emitted.

SCALE: mean_vector_norm is a raw Euclidean norm of a mean difference, not an effect size -- it ignores within-class covariance, so overlapping noisy classes can outscore cleanly separated low-variance ones, and it spans 15x between two models of identical depth and width.
NAMING: the task name conflates Ilharco et al.'s weight-space tau = theta_ft - theta_pre with Zou et al.'s activation-space reading direction; only the latter is computed.
fix: No implementation fix outstanding. On the comparability axis: (1) register a normalized twin for max_norm_layer only alongside a disclosure that the depth FRACTION is 1.0 in 9 of 10 models, so the twin does not by itself make the column usable -- prefer dropping it or replacing it with an argmax over a per-model standardised profile; (2) for a scale-free strength replace mean_vector_norm with a regularised pooled-covariance effect D^2 = (mu+ - mu-)^T Sigma^-1 (mu+ - mu-); (3) ship a random-weight control column, since an untrained GPT-2 currently reports the same max_norm_layer and a mean_vector_norm within 11% of the trained model; (4) rename the task repe_clustermean_reading_direction and reserve task_vector for Ilharco's weight-space object. NORMALIZED-VARIANT AXIS (measured 2026-09-04): the surviving registered twin, mean_vector_norm/sqrt(d_model), is RED. First, it is redundant: it is bit-identical to the in-task mean_vector_norm_normalized on all 20 models measured, so registering it only adds a perfectly collinear column. Second, sqrt(d_model) is not the term that makes this column incomparable. A task vector is a difference of residual-stream activations and the residual scale is a free reparameterisation: multiplying pythia-70m's embed_in and every block's output projection (attention.dense, mlp.dense_4h_to_h, weights and biases) by c = 2 multiplies the residual norm at every block by 2.00000-2.00807 while the logits move by rel 1.4e-04 and the argmax agrees on 100.00% of positions -- so both the raw column and its sqrt(d) twin double for a model computing exactly the same function. Third, it barely reduces the measured association: 66-model archive +0.538/+0.614 (d_model/n_layers) -> +0.388/+0.509, and 20 fresh models +0.050/+0.697 (p = 6e-04) -> -0.051/+0.676 (p = 1e-03), i.e. the depth term is untouched. A scale-free strength must be a RATIO to something that scales the same way (e.g. ||v||/||h|| at the same layer), as the fix above already suggests.
fix_applied: R24: REMOVED the max_norm_layer normalized twin -- after the hook fix max_norm_layer/(L-1) = 1.0 in 9 of 10 panel models, so the twin is a near-constant while the raw column is a pure depth readout (rho +0.997). Per the review it should be dropped or replaced by the argmax of a per-model standardised profile.
